comparison: Perfect agreement on lipid enrichment analysis (C47-C50). Both evaluations find the coarse-grained simulation methodology and lipid fingerprint analysis appropriate and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes clear methodology and statistical thresholds, while peer review affirms the multiscale simulation approach as 'extremely appropriate.'

Perfect agreement on mutational validation (C67). Both find the computational mutagenesis supports the binding site identification. Peer review initially requested this as a weakness, then confirmed concerns were addressed. OpenEval notes experimental validation would strengthen findings but accepts computational evidence as supportive.

Perfect agreement on atomistic simulation findings (C68-C75). Both evaluations strongly support the detailed interaction analysis and differential phosphate roles. Peer review explicitly affirms atomistic simulations as advisable to confirm coarse-grained results. OpenEval highlights robust statistical analysis from 7.5 μs total simulation time.

Perfect agreement on state-dependent binding (C84-C87). Both find the comparative analysis across Nav1.7 structures convincing and well-documented. OpenEval notes uncertainty about resting state model, but peer review accepts state dependence as compelling evidence supporting the mechanistic model.

Strong agreement on PI(4)P vs PI(4,5)P2 comparison (C101-C105, with C100 overlap). Both find the comparative binding data well-supported and mechanistic interpretation reasonable. Peer review notes lack of experimental validation as limitation but finds results 'compelling and believable.' OpenEval similarly notes mechanistic details remain inferential but well-supported.

Strong agreement on PIP binding site identification (C55-C66, with C51-C54 also in peer R1). Both evaluations strongly support the DIV S4-S5 linker binding findings. OpenEval emphasizes robust statistics from 156 binding events and notes unexpected PIP3 behavior. Peer review finds simulations 'convincing' with all reviewers explicitly affirming these findings.

Agreement on occupancy analysis (C51-C54). OpenEval finds clear statistical support with >80% occupancy threshold and specificity analysis. Peer review includes these claims in broader affirmation of PIP binding findings at DIV S4-S5 linker, noting 'thorough set of analysis' demonstrating PIP-protein interactions.

Partial disagreement on therapeutic implications (C78-C80, with C10 overlap). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C80 about 'partial rescue' requires experimental validation despite supporting simulation data. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting competitive binding mechanism as key finding. Both acknowledge speculative nature but differ on confidence level.

Agreement on linker mobility reduction (C76-C77, with C11-C12 in peer review). Both find RMSF analysis convincing evidence that PIP2 reduces DIV S4-S5 and DIII-IV linker mobility. OpenEval notes timescale limitations (1.5 μs vs millisecond biology). Peer review states authors 'convincingly showed' this slows recovery conformational changes.

Disagreement on resting state findings (C88-C91, with C14-C15 in peer review). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to acknowledged uncertainty in resting state model lacking experimental structure. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting gating charge binding and activation impediment as key findings despite model limitations.

Agreement on disease relevance (C93-C95, with C92 overlap). Both find disease mutation connections supported by conservation analysis. OpenEval notes C95 is speculative interpretation without direct experimental evidence. Peer review accepts disease connections as relevant context for therapeutic implications without challenging the claims.

Agreement on conservation analysis (C82-C83, C96). Both support structural alignment and sequence conservation findings. OpenEval notes functional significance requires experimental validation. Peer review emphasizes broader applicability to other ion channels and accepts conservation as supporting generalizability.

Disagreement on mechanistic hypotheses (C10, C15). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting these are hypotheses requiring experimental validation despite plausible simulation support. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting competitive binding mechanism (C10) as demonstrated key finding rather than hypothesis.

Disagreement on gating charge mechanism (C15). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN hypothesis requiring validation. Peer review (R6) rates as SUPPORTED, with editor and reviewers accepting that PIP binding to gating charges may impede activation as a key finding rather than speculative mechanism.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background claims (C1-C3, C16-C38) about Nav channels as SUPPORTED by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background context.

OpenEval evaluated prior experimental work citations (C4-C6, C44-C46, C100) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R10 includes C100 but focuses on comparative interpretation rather than citation validation. Background citations not separately evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluated comparative PIP interaction literature (C39-C43) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent contextual background rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.
